name: M5Stack ATOM Lite (ESP32-PICO-D4)
radio: the SoC's own radios: wifi24, ble, btclassic

flash.bootloader_instructions: Plug in; the CH9102 bridge puts the chip in download mode by itself (DTR/RTS). If that fails, hold the front button (GPIO39) while plugging in.
flash.note: Values from public documentation; not yet verified on a board of this kind (the target is experimental until then).

led.note: one SK6812/WS2812 RGB LED on GPIO27 (kitsune: FastLED, brightness 20)

battery.divider_note: Powered from USB or a 5 V pack. kitsune's note: the pack must not have a low-current cut-off, or the board never wakes from deep sleep.

notes: The only kitsune board with Bluetooth Classic (original ESP32); kitsune pins its BT Classic project to the Arduino core 2.x for Bluedroid.
ESP32 (not S3/C3): the second-stage bootloader lives at 0x1000, so a merged image starts there.
Power: kitsune foxes sleep between transmissions; a USB power bank with a low-current auto-off cuts power during the sleep and the fox never wakes (kitsune's README). Use a pack without auto-off.
Serial: through the CH9102 bridge, so the console stays up through sleep — the only kitsune board where it does (kitsune's README).

serial.notes: kitsune prints 'ESP32 boot count', 'Awake and screaming', 'Going to sleep' and 'PANIC' on its serial port; no command interface.
